title.narrative: Strengthening Inclusive Disaster Risk Governance for Climate Resilience in Asia
Strengthening Inclusive Disaster Risk Governance for Climate Resilience in Asia

description.narrative:
Strengthening Inclusive Disaster Risk Governance for Climate Resilience in Asia is a collaboration between the International Rescue Committee (IRC), Duryog Nivaran and the Asia Disaster Reduction and Response Network (ADRN). The intervention will last for 4.5 years. IRC is the leading organization in the consortium and is the agreement partner to Sida. The main geographic focus of the programme is South Asia and Southeast Asia.
The consortium will strengthen the resilience of communities at risk to climate change. This will be achieved by: (1) strengthening regional networks of civil society organizations to achieve inclusive climate change adaptation and disaster risk reduction; (2) mitigating power imbalances that lead to increased climate and disaster risks facing women, men, girls, and boys and other at-risk groups; and (3) helping communities, local governments, and other stakeholders to take sustainable local-level adaptive actions and contribute to environmental sustainability.

Strengthening Inclusive Disaster Risk Governance for Climate Resilience in Asia är ett samarbete mellan International Rescue Committee (IRC), Duryog Nivaran och Asia Disaster Reduction and Response Network (ADRN). Interventionen ska pågå I 4,5 år. IRC är den ledande organisationen i konsortiet och är avtalspartner till Sida. Insatsens geografiska fokus är Sydasien och Sydostasien.
Insatsen kommer att stärka motståndskraft för klimatförändring. Detta kommer att uppnås genom: (1) stärkt regionala nätverk av civilsamhällsorganisationer som bidrar till klimatanpassning och katastrofsriskreducering; (2) minskade ojämställdhet mellan kvinnor, män, flickor och pojkar samt andra utsätta grupper inom deras klimatarbete; och (3) stärkta möjligheter för samhällena och lokala myndigheterna att vidta hållbara anpassningsåtgärder på lokal nivå.

The information below reflects progress achieved prior to the phase-out of programme implementation in June 2026. Up to that point, the SIDRRA project had delivered a range of expected results consistent with its theory of change, while also generating several positive and unanticipated outcomes.
Improved Reach and Participation of At-Risk Groups:
The project directly reached 9,384 people, including 5,058 women and 4,326 men. Participation from marginalized and at-risk groups was substantial, including 1,105 Indigenous Peoples, 758 Dalit community members, 153 persons with disabilities, and 405 members of religious minority groups.
Strengthened Inclusive Disaster Risk Governance:
Consortium members strengthened their governance and institutional systems, including safeguarding, Monitoring, Evaluation, Accountability and Learning (MEAL), communications, and financial management. Community Disaster Risk Reduction and Management (DRRM) groups were formally recognized by local authorities, enhancing their institutional legitimacy and role in local governance. Local governments increasingly engaged with community-generated evidence and locally led adaptation solutions, contributing to improved vertical accountability and more inclusive disaster risk governance.
Enhanced Gender Equality and Social Inclusion:
Women, Indigenous Peoples, youth, and persons with disabilities played a more active role in disaster risk governance and decision-making processes, reflecting stronger implementation of a Human Rights-Based Approach (HRBA) and gender-responsive programming.
Local-Led Adaptation and Action:
The project supported 11 locally led adaptation and disaster risk governance actions across 6 countries, demonstrating practical implementation of resilience-building solutions.
Unexpected Results:
The consortium achieved more substantial improvements in governance, MEAL, safeguarding, and financial management systems than originally anticipated. These enhancements extend beyond typical project-level capacity building, establishing a stronger institutional foundation for sustained regional collaboration and long-term organizational resilience.
Through an adaptive and opportunistic networking approach, the project achieved higher-than-expected regional visibility and engagement in policy processes. This resulted in stronger thematic hubs, expanded consortium membership, and increased influence at the regional level, representing an emergent systems-level outcome.
